signals.title: @blaiseaguera: Project Maven: A Marine Colonel, His Team, and the Dawn of AI Warfare by @KatrinaManson In the beginning, Project Maven, formally the “Algor
signals.content: Project Maven: A Marine Colonel, His Team, and the Dawn of AI Warfare by @KatrinaManson In the beginning, Project Maven, formally the “Algorithmic Warfare Cross-Functional Team,” was the brainchild of Drew Cukor, a maverick Marine Corps colonel. He understood, as many of his peers in military leadership didn’t back in 2017, that AI would transform war, just as it would transform every domain in which complex decisions must continually be made based on flows of incoming information (which is, yes, almost every domain in modern life). Along with many colleagues, I first learned about Maven in the context of the 2018 protests at Google that resulted in the company stepping away from the project—a move welcomed by the many other tech companies eager to take those contracts. Now, eight years on and nearly five years after the invasion of Ukraine, I understand a good deal more. Although Manson’s views are at times evident, this is no polemic. Her book is a thoroughly researched history, built on years of reporting and extensive access to key people. The topic is vitally important and defies any simplistic moral analysis. War sucks. As the mechanized horrors of World War I made clear, “efficient” war sucks even more. So does being unprepared.

Title: xianwins4ever-ux/sound-skill

Brief: This repository provides an AI agent sound‑retrieval skill that aggregates four public audio sources—Pixabay, Freesound, Mixkit, and Kenney. It also incorporates the capabilities claimed by the paid version of vibe‑motion. The author has open‑sourced the project, and the current fork consolidates the original code while fixing 25 reported bugs. signals.content: BlackSky acquires @EpochGeo to expand real-time intelligence capabilities. The geospatial data science firm specializes specializes in artificial intelligence and machine learning solutions that fuse multiple data sources for mission-critical defense applications. The acquisition advances BlackSky's strategy to deliver comprehensive solutions for real-time intelligence on the most important locations and events that are consequential to national and economic security. “The acquisition of EpochGeo brings exceptional technology, world-class expertise and customer mission experience that will help accelerate our real-time intelligence capabilities,” said Brian O’Toole, BlackSky CEO. “The next evolution of the industry is the integration, fusion and analysis of a wide range of space-based and terrestrial data sources that enable us to rapidly see, understand and respond to relevant change in real-time.” Read the full announcement: https://t.co/roJt4GaHvl
signals.score_reason: Twitter/X discussion signal; strategic/security relevance. Final score: 52. Freshness: source age 0.51d.
signals.brief_en: BlackSky announced the acquisition of EpochGeo, a geospatial data‑science firm that develops AI and machine learning tools to fuse multiple data streams for defense‑grade, mission‑critical applications. The deal supports BlackSky’s roadmap to provide end‑to‑end, real‑time intelligence on locations and events that affect national and economic security. CEO Brian O’Toole said the purchase adds technology, expertise and customer experience that will accelerate BlackSky’s real‑time intelligence capabilities.
